- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, particularly after mid-forecast period.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent downward momentum — if last 5–7 days show falling prices, forecast should not continue upward.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values show sharp drops or sudden reversals.
- Model tends to “smooth” sharp transitions — e.g., a sudden drop from 80 to 60 is often forecasted as a gradual decline rather than a sharp drop.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices — if last 3–5 days are above 75, forecast often peaks too high and then drops too fast.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns — e.g., end-of-month or end-of-quarter corrections are often missed.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price direction — often forecasts 1–2 days behind actual trend reversal.
- Model tends to overfit recent high values — if last 10 days are high, model may overpredict future highs, ignoring mean reversion.
